blindSummary:
This is a hazardous destination for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct between civilians is legal, but strikingly, two code provisions still criminalise it for police and armed-forces members — challenged at the constitutional court in August 2024, revealing the institutional culture. There is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination law covering SOGI (a foreign government formally recommended one at the 2024 UN periodic review), and documented violence against trans women is high, particularly affecting the most marginalised.

The main beach-resort destinations are heavily insulated resort enclaves with international norms; the capital has a visible community and an annual Pride caravan. Outside those bubbles, strongly patriarchal norms, police harassment of trans women (especially sex workers), and hostility toward dark-skinned people bound up with the neighbouring state's migrant population are documented as compounding for dark-skinned trans people.
blindOutOfScope: The police/military sodomy articles do not apply to civilians or visitors; resort vs. non-resort risk differs sharply.
blindSourceSummaries: An international rights group (Aug 2024): this country's constitutional court reviews penal-code provisions criminalising same-sex conduct.

UN periodic-review record (46th session, April 2024): a recommending state urged this country to criminalise discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity and to ensure the right of trans and intersex persons to change name and gender in the civil registry - the recommendation was accepted.

A news magazine's interview with an international rights organisation (March 2019) marking a transgender-visibility day - including a trans activist from this country sharing her story of trans life and activism there.
An overseas LGBT news outlet (Apr 2017): government officials from this country speak at an LGBT rights conference.
An overseas LGBT news outlet (Apr 2016): opinion piece arguing attacks on the country's openly gay foreign ambassador are attacks on LGBT people there.
An overseas LGBT news outlet (Apr 2017): the departure of this country's openly gay foreign ambassador leaves an advocacy void.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition and no SOGI anti-discrimination law — resident-facing gaps; the police/military sodomy articles apply to residents in uniform, not civilians or visitors.
